chapter: Blackbirds, Carmen Jones and the Ziegfeld Follies
title: Home from England: Loew's State and paying their own passage
summary: Nazarro's telegram about a picture came in 1936; in the earlier trip they paid their own fare and played Loew's State.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: before we got to America at that time -- the manager, Nazarro, had sent a telegram for us to come back because he had a picture for us, picture contract for us -- no, it couldn't have been in 1930. It wasn't that, he didn't have it in 1930 -- come on back to America. But he didn't have no picture for us then, it was in '36 he had the picture.

So we come back to America after we did that and we opened up the Loews Circuit, Loews Theater in New York. Loews State Theater in New York. We played there. And while we were playing at Loews State Theater --
He sent you a telegram to come back?
No, not that one. Later on he did that. Later on he sent the message. It was in '36 he sent the message.
It was on your own motivation to go back, you were tired of it.
Yeah, it was only a two weeks' contract anyway. I was ready to go back anyway. And I paid for the transpor-

tation because we paid for the transportation to come out of our salary. So I didn't have any money left. I just paid for the tickets to come on back. And we started over in those Loews Theaters in New York when we got back and it was in 1931 when we went into Ziegfeld Follies. And to get in the Follies there was a show there that everybody wanted to play in, they would go on for nothing. Everybody wanted to go in the Ziegfeld Follies then, you know.
